newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares in record territory pre-bourse.
newsitem.headline: German shares in record territory pre-bourse.

text.p: German shares traded in or around record territory on Wednesday, as a strong close on Wall Street overnight and a strengthening dollar boosted sentiment on the IBIS DAX index.
The index of electronic trade was up around half a percent, or 18.67 points, at 3,684.10 points, while the June DAX future contract was up 17 points at 3,691.

"Wall Street was up yesterday and it looks like we're trying to emulate that good order flow here. This is not a down day and I think it's very possible that we could break 3,700 points today," said a Frankfurt broker.
"There is a lot of merger talk out there today, especially since Roche bought Boehringer Mannheim the other day, and people are looking at the banking sector closely," he said.

One of the main engines behind the advance was industrial giant Daimler Benz. It was one of the volume leaders early on and advanced strongly after it said it expected "substantial" increases in 1997 sales and operating profits.
The share rose to a high of 137.45 marks at one point, before falling back to 136.75 marks later, up 65 pfennigs.
"The Daimler sales figures for the first four months did not disappoint and were well received," a trader said.
Shares in insurer Allianz AG rose after it said it expected its premium income to rise around 11 percent to around 83 billion marks in 1997 and said it expected moderate double-digit growth in 1997.
The share rose 4.50 marks to a new high of 383.50 marks, jumping 3.50 marks after the announcement.

Floor-covering manufacturer Tarkett saw its shares advance nearly 12 percent to 33.50 marks after it said it was merging its worldwide floor covering business with that of French group Sommer Allibert Sa.
